title: Mapping London's Hidden River
paras: In nineteenth-century London, the sewer map became an instrument of government. Earlier drains had carried human [[excrement|excrement]] towards the Thames, the same river from which water companies drew supplies. What a [[mariner|mariner]] encountered as a navigable channel, a sanitary engineer increasingly understood as the exposed artery of a dangerously interconnected city.

The Great Stink of 1858 made that connection politically intolerable. River odours penetrated Parliament, lending urgency to proposals whose expense had previously seemed [[ruinous|ruinous]]. Campaigners could invest accounts of crowded courts and polluted water with considerable [[pathos|pathos]]; opponents could [[sneer|sneer]] at costly engineering ambitions. Yet the smell made postponement harder to defend, and legislation enabled an extensive reconstruction.

Under Joseph Bazalgette, intercepting sewers redirected waste downstream rather than allowing it to enter the river throughout central London. Progress on their construction was far from [[meteoric|meteoric]]: major works extended across years. Plans translated gradients, brick tunnels and pumping stations into lines on [[pliable|pliable]] paper. Their orderly appearance could have a [[subliminal|subliminal]] reassuring effect, making a contested intervention seem almost inevitable.

The system offered substantial [[deliverance|deliverance]] from the city's accumulated filth, although moving sewage downstream did not make it disappear. Its [[epoch-making|epoch-making]] significance lay partly in scale: sanitation became a coordinated metropolitan undertaking rather than a patchwork of drains. The map's neat lines thus recorded something larger than buried masonry—the emergence of public responsibility for what households wished merely to flush away.
zh: 在十九世纪的伦敦，下水道地图成为了一种治理工具。早期的排水沟将人类排泄物排向泰晤士河，而供水公司也从这条河中取水。在海员眼中可以通航的水道，在卫生工程师看来，却日益成为一座各部分紧密相连、危险相互传递的城市所暴露在外的动脉。
1858年的“大恶臭”事件使这种关联在政治上再也无法容忍。河水的臭气侵入议会，使那些此前被认为开支可能造成严重财政损失的方案显得更加紧迫。改革倡导者描述拥挤的院落和受污染的水源，能够唤起强烈的悲悯；反对者则可能嘲讽耗资巨大的工程雄心。然而，臭气让拖延更难自圆其说，随后通过的立法为大规模改建铺平了道路。
在约瑟夫·巴泽尔杰特的主持下，截流下水道将污水引向下游，而不再任其沿伦敦市中心各处流入河中。工程推进远非突飞猛进：主要工程持续了多年。设计图将坡度、砖砌隧道和泵站转化为柔韧纸张上的线条。这些图纸井然有序的外观，可能在人们未曾察觉时起到安抚作用，让一项备受争议的干预措施显得几乎势在必行。
这套系统使城市在很大程度上摆脱了积存的污秽，尽管把污水移往下游并不意味着让它消失。其划时代的意义部分在于规模：卫生设施建设不再是零散排水沟的拼凑，而成为整个都市协同推进的事业。因此，地图上整齐的线条记录了超越地下砖石工程的变化——对于住户只想一冲了之的废物，公共责任开始确立。

q.s: The water companies drawing supplies from the Thames were publicly owned.
q.why: 首段未说明供水公司的所有权归属。

q.s: Odours from the river entered Parliament during the Great Stink.
q.why: 第二段明确说河水臭气侵入了议会。

q.s: The principal sewer construction works were completed in less than a year.
q.why: 原文明确说主要工程持续了多年。
